rationale: Evidence: all 60 development trials ended off_track with progress 0.10-0.15 and one line-loss event each. The robot leaves the tape early and never recovers. The off-track limit here is max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06 m, and max_error sits at about 0.06, so the robot runs off at the first sharp bend. rms_error (0.026-0.030) is small, so the robot tracks the line well until the first bend. The failure is a loss of tracking margin on bends at speed, not steady-state error. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.6 -> 1.3, so the robot can turn within the gain it has. (2) kp 2.0 -> 4.0, because at kp 2 a full-scale signal gives only about 700 PWM of wheel differential, which is too weak to pull the robot back from the edge on tight bends. (3) kd 0.2 -> 0.5 to damp the faster steering response, and ki 0.05 -> 0.02 to limit integral overshoot. (4) sensor_size 0.012 -> 0.016. A larger footprint keeps at least one sensor on the 25 mm tape when the robot is off-centre, which should reduce the early line-loss events. Sensor positions, weights, wheel geometry and line_loss are unchanged so the effect of the gain and speed change is isolated. Expected result: fewer line-loss events, progress above 0.5 on the oval and s-bend, and the first completions on some seeds. Risk: a higher kp may cause oscillation on the slalom, which steering_oscillation will show. Hypotheses for next iteration: if the robot still leaves on the first bend, reduce base_speed further; if it wobbles, raise kd or lower kp; if it completes but is slow, raise base_speed. Measurements requested: progress and completion_time (for speed), line_loss_events and max_error (for recovery), steering_oscillation (for gain stability).
